title: Uint8Array crossing chrome.runtime.sendMessage arrives as a plain {index: byte} object — rehydrate on the receive side
trigger: Binary payloads (Uint8Array, audio/image bytes) are returned through chrome.runtime.sendMessage from service worker to page/content script
principle: Chrome runtime messaging JSON-serializes the response — a Uint8Array arrives as {0:73, 1:68, ...} (plain object, length preserved via numeric keys). new Blob([obj]) produces '[object Object]' text; new Uint8Array(obj) yields an empty array — the audio 'loads' but is unplayable, with no thrown error. Rehydrate at the receive boundary: instanceof check → Uint8Array.from(Object.values(v)) for numeric-keyed objects. Zod schemas validating instanceof Uint8Array pass on the sender side but the wire still degrades the type — schema validation cannot catch transport degradation.

cases.context: FETCH_LOCAL_AUDIO returned AudioItem[] with audioBytes: Uint8Array. The SW-side FetchLocalAudioResponseSchema.parse passed, but the popup received {0:73,1:68,...} → blob URL wrapped garbage bytes → tester fell back to Wiktionary despite bytes being fully present (2725/2725, ID3 magic intact).
cases.bad:
const blob = new Blob([item.audioBytes], { type: 'audio/mpeg' });
// item.audioBytes is {0:73,1:68,...} → blob contains literal '[object Object]'

applyFor: Any chrome.runtime.sendMessage response carrying Uint8Array/ArrayBuffer/typed arrays
Media pipelines that turn received bytes into Blob/object URLs
New message types returning binary payloads — add a wire-shape regression test ({0:..,1:..} fixture)
